# OpenClaw Complete Skill Catalog & Knowledge Base
> Last updated: 2026-04-03
> Total skills listed: 71 | Categories: 10 | Articles: 45 | Tutorials: 5 | Glossary terms: 20

## Site Information
- Name: ClawSkills  
- URL: https://openclaw-skillshub.com
- Purpose: The definitive directory for OpenClaw AI agent skills
- Install any skill: `npx clawhub@latest install <skill-name>`

## Quick Facts
- Framework: OpenClaw (open-source, MIT license, 150K+ GitHub stars)
- Supported OS: macOS, Linux, Windows WSL
- Supported LLMs: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Mistral, Cohere, Ollama
- Trust tiers: Verified (security-audited), Community (peer-reviewed), Unreviewed

---

## Glossary

- **OpenClaw**: OpenClaw is an open-source framework for building, deploying, and managing autonomous AI agents that execute complex workflows across tools and services. → https://openclaw-skillshub.com/glossary/what-is-openclaw
- **OpenClaw Skills**: OpenClaw Skills are modular, composable plugins that extend AI agent capabilities with specific tools, integrations, and workflows. → https://openclaw-skillshub.com/glossary/what-are-openclaw-skills
- **OpenClaw vs Other AI Agent Frameworks**: OpenClaw differentiates from other AI agent frameworks through its modular skill-based architecture, massive community ecosystem, and production-first design philosophy. → https://openclaw-skillshub.com/glossary/openclaw-vs-other-frameworks
- **RAG Pipeline**: A RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) pipeline is an AI architecture that retrieves relevant documents from a knowledge base and feeds them as context to a large language model to produce accurate, grounded responses. → https://openclaw-skillshub.com/glossary/what-is-rag-pipeline
- **Prompt Chaining**: Prompt chaining is an AI workflow pattern where the output of one LLM prompt is used as input for the next, enabling complex multi-step reasoning and task decomposition. → https://openclaw-skillshub.com/glossary/what-is-prompt-chaining
- **AI Agent**: An AI agent is an autonomous software system powered by large language models that can perceive its environment, reason about tasks, use tools, and take actions to achieve specified goals with minimal human intervention. → https://openclaw-skillshub.com/glossary/what-is-ai-agent
- **LLM Routing**: LLM routing is a technique that automatically selects the optimal language model for each query based on factors like complexity, cost, latency requirements, and task type. → https://openclaw-skillshub.com/glossary/what-is-llm-routing
- **Vector Embedding**: A vector embedding is a dense numerical representation (array of floating-point numbers) that captures the semantic meaning of text, images, or other data, enabling similarity search and machine learning operations. → https://openclaw-skillshub.com/glossary/what-is-vector-embedding
- **SKILL.md**: SKILL.md is the declarative manifest file that defines an OpenClaw skill's name, description, permissions, tools, and behavioral instructions. → https://openclaw-skillshub.com/glossary/what-is-skill-md
- **MCP Server**: An MCP (Model Context Protocol) server is a standalone process that exposes tools, resources, and prompts to AI agents via a standardized JSON-RPC protocol. → https://openclaw-skillshub.com/glossary/what-is-mcp-server
- **Agent Sandboxing**: Agent sandboxing is the practice of isolating AI agents within restricted execution environments to prevent unintended or malicious actions on the host system. → https://openclaw-skillshub.com/glossary/what-is-agent-sandboxing
- **Prompt Injection**: Prompt injection is an attack technique where malicious instructions are inserted into an AI agent's input to manipulate its behavior, bypass safety controls, or exfiltrate data. → https://openclaw-skillshub.com/glossary/what-is-prompt-injection
- **Tool Calling**: Tool calling (also called function calling) is the ability of an LLM to invoke external functions, APIs, or system commands as part of its reasoning and response generation. → https://openclaw-skillshub.com/glossary/what-is-tool-calling
- **Agent Memory**: Agent memory is the ability of an AI agent to store, retrieve, and use information from past interactions, enabling contextual awareness and learning over time. → https://openclaw-skillshub.com/glossary/what-is-agent-memory
- **LLM Orchestration**: LLM orchestration is the coordination of multiple language model calls, tool invocations, and control flow decisions into coherent multi-step AI agent workflows. → https://openclaw-skillshub.com/glossary/what-is-llm-orchestration
- **ClawHub**: ClawHub is the official package registry for OpenClaw skills, providing centralized distribution, versioning, and discovery of SKILL.md-based agent capabilities. → https://openclaw-skillshub.com/glossary/what-is-clawhub
- **OpenClaw Permissions**: OpenClaw permissions are declarations in SKILL.md files that specify which system resources (filesystem, network, environment variables) a skill is allowed to access. → https://openclaw-skillshub.com/glossary/what-is-openclaw-permissions
- **Multi-Agent System**: A multi-agent system is an AI architecture where multiple specialized agents collaborate, delegate tasks, and communicate to solve problems beyond a single agent's capability. → https://openclaw-skillshub.com/glossary/what-is-multi-agent-system
- **Context Window**: The context window is the maximum number of tokens that a language model can process in a single interaction, including both input and output. → https://openclaw-skillshub.com/glossary/what-is-context-window
- **AI Guardrails**: AI guardrails are safety mechanisms — input validators, output filters, and behavioral constraints — that prevent AI agents from producing harmful outputs or taking dangerous actions. → https://openclaw-skillshub.com/glossary/what-are-ai-guardrails
